statement: Whenever the function returns a result r (i.e., Ok r), let ys be the sequence of values in r. Then len(ys) = n, and for every j with 0 <= j < n / k (integer division) and every p with 0 <= p < k, we have ys[j*k + p] = xs[j*k + (k-1-p)], and for every i with k*(n/k) <= i < n, we have ys[i] = xs[i].
preconditions: Let n be the number of nodes in head, and let xs be the sequence of values in head (so xs[0] is the value of the first node, xs[1] the second, etc., and len(xs) = n). The preconditions are: 1 <= k, k <= n, n <= 5000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= xs[i] <= 1000.

statement: Whenever the function returns Ok r, the multiset of values in r equals the multiset of values in head. That is, for every integer v, the number of occurrences of v in r equals the number of occurrences of v in head.
preconditions: Let n be the number of nodes in head, and let xs be the sequence of values in head. The preconditions are: 1 <= k, k <= n, n <= 5000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= xs[i] <= 1000.

statement: For every input (head, k) satisfying the preconditions, if the function returns Ok r on (head, k) and returns Ok r2 on (r, k), then r2 = head.
preconditions: Let n be the number of nodes in head, and let xs be the sequence of values in head. The preconditions are: 1 <= k, k <= n, n <= 5000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= xs[i] <= 1000.

statement: Whenever the function returns Ok r, there exists a sequence of lists B_0, ..., B_{m-1} and a list T such that: head = B_0 ++ ... ++ B_{m-1} ++ T, for every j with 0 <= j < m, len(B_j) = k, len(T) < k, and r = reverse(B_0) ++ ... ++ reverse(B_{m-1}) ++ T, where m = n / k (integer division).
preconditions: Let n be the number of nodes in head, and let xs be the sequence of values in head. The preconditions are: 1 <= k, k <= n, n <= 5000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= xs[i] <= 1000.
